import unicodedata


def slugify(value: str) -> str:
    \"\"\"Return a URL-friendly ASCII slug.\"\"\"

    normalized = unicodedata.normalize(\"NFKD\", value)
    ascii_value = normalized.encode(\"ascii\", \"ignore\").decode(\"ascii\")

tasks.name: Repair JSON CLI
tasks.title: Repair JSON CLI
tasks.instruction: Repair greet.py so `python greet.py Ada --repeat 3` writes exactly one compact JSON object to stdout: {"greeting":"Hello, Ada!","repeat":3}. The greeting must use the supplied name and repeat must be a JSON integer. Preserve the command-line interface, use only the standard library, and run the tests before finishing.

files.content:
import argparse


def main() -> None:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("name")
    parser.add_argument("--repeat", type=int, default=1)
    args = parser.parse_args()
    print({"message": f"Hello {args.name}", "repeat": str(args.repeat)})


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

import json
import subprocess
import sys
import unittest


class GreetCliTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def run_cli(self, *arguments: str) -> str:
        completed = subprocess.run(
            [sys.executable, "greet.py", *arguments],
            check=True,
            capture_output=True,
            text=True,
        )
        self.assertEqual(completed.stderr, "")
        return completed.stdout

    def test_compact_json_contract(self) -> None:
        output = self.run_cli("Ada", "--repeat", "3")
        self.assertEqual(output, '{"greeting":"Hello, Ada!","repeat":3}\n')
        self.assertEqual(
            json.loads(output),
            {"greeting": "Hello, Ada!", "repeat": 3},
        )

    def test_name_is_not_hard_coded(self) -> None:
        payload = json.loads(self.run_cli("Grace", "--repeat", "1"))
        self.assertEqual(payload["greeting"], "Hello, Grace!")
        self.assertIsInstance(payload["repeat"], int)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()
